newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Oman oil expansion delayed by three months - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Oman oil expansion delayed by three months - MEES.

text.p: Petroleum Development Oman's (PDO) plans to lift its output to 850,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September have been delayed until the end of this year, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

"PDO had hoped to hit the 850,000 bpd mark by September but operators have encountered delays delivering rigs and other technical problems which...have had the cumulative effect of setting back the expansion project," MEES reported.
PDO is the main oil operator in non-OPEC member Oman and is currently producing around 830,000 bpd, 30,000 bpd higher than since the start of the year.

"It appears that Petroleum Development Oman will not be able to reach its 1996 production target of 850,000 bpd until the end of the year, some three months later than originally planned," MEES reported.
Delays in supplies from non-OPEC producers has been a factor in the recent strength in crude prices ahead of the northern hemisphere's winter.
